title: B1 scope verification treated untracked Python bytecode as a Worker source change
discovered_by: actual Phase F B1 R5 run
symptom: R03 created only allowed fixture outputs, but B1 blocked before public Checks because importing a public checker generated benchmark_checks/__pycache__/check_profile_r.cpython-312.pyc outside the Task write scope
reproduction: Use FakeRuntime to create an untracked benchmark_checks/__pycache__/*.pyc beside an allowed src/** change

evidence.detail: R5 attempt_finished recorded scope_violation with the sole out-of-scope path benchmark_checks/__pycache__/check_profile_r.cpython-312.pyc

root_cause: The independent Judge normalized untracked Python bytecode before scope evaluation, but the B1 scheduler applied scope validation directly to Git changes without the same transient-file normalization

considered_options.reason: would hide arbitrary non-bytecode files written outside the Task scope
the Worker can invoke its own Python subprocess before Controller Checks and the scope verifier must classify observed files safely

considered_options.option: remove only untracked regular __pycache__/*.pyc files without symlink or junction components
considered_options.reason: removes the observed interpreter byproduct while preserving tracked bytecode and arbitrary-file scope enforcement

resolution: Normalize only untracked regular __pycache__/*.pyc files before B1 declared-artifact and write-scope verification, then recalculate changed paths; keep ordinary files in the same directory visible to scope validation
verification: Fake bytecode normalization and ordinary-file rejection tests: 2 passed
No model, SDK, Codex, Docker, or network call was used for the correction verification
remaining_risks: The sealed R5 result remains blocked and is not rewritten; a fresh R6 live run needs separate model-use approval
